rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a disease affecting plants.

example.english: These tomatoes have developed blight, and their leaves are starting to turn yellow.
example.traditional: 呢啲番茄出現植物病，葉都開始枯黃喇。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 faan1 ke2 ceot1 jin6 zik6 mat6 beng6 jip6 dou1 hoi1 ci2 fu1 wong4 laa3

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice for damaging someone's prospects or quality of life.

example.english: The company's sudden move can blight our family's livelihood.
example.traditional: 公司突然搬走，真係可以影響我哋一家嘅生計。
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 dat6 jin4 bun1 zau2 zan1 hai6 ho2 ji5 jing2 hoeng2 ngo5 dei6 jat1 gaa1 ge3 sang1 gai3

rows.note: Use this colloquial choice when you mean actively ruining or spoiling something.

example.english: Changing things randomly like that will blight the whole project.
example.traditional: 你咁樣亂咁改，直頭搞衰晒成件事。
example.jyutping: nei5 gam2 joeng2 lyun6 gam3 goi2 zik6 tau4 gaau2 seoi1 saai3 seng4 gin6 si6

rows.note: Use this when the emphasis is on holding back development or progress.

example.english: Such high rents blight young people's chances of buying a home.
example.traditional: 房租咁貴，真係阻住後生仔置業。
example.jyutping: fong4 zou1 gam3 gwai3 zan1 hai6 zo2 zyu6 hau6 saang1 zai2 zi3 jip6

rows.note: Use this for a harmful thing or force that holds back progress or damages life metaphorically.

example.english: Gambling addiction is a blight on families and makes everyone unhappy.
example.traditional: 沉迷賭博係家庭嘅禍害，搞到大家都唔開心。
example.jyutping: cam4 mai4 dou2 bok3 hai6 gaa1 ting4 ge3 wo6 hoi6 gaau2 dou3 daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 hoi1 sam1

rows.note: Use this specifically for the rundown and unsightly condition of a city or urban district.

example.english: The area's urban blight is worsening after years of poor planning.
example.traditional: 該區長期缺乏規劃，市區衰敗日益嚴重。
example.jyutping: goi1 keoi1 coeng4 kei4 kyut3 fat6 kwai1 waak6 si5 keoi1 seoi1 baai6 jat6 jik1 jim4 zung6
